intro: Backpacks end up on the floor because the storage is too far from the door or too hard to use. Put the storage where bags land, at a height the owner can reach, and give each person a defined spot. Measure the wall, door and floor space before buying, check the weight rating, since a loaded bag can weigh 15 pounds or more, and use studs or proper anchors for anything wall-mounted. If you rent, choose no-drill options such as over-the-door racks, stands and bins.

picks.description: A row of sturdy hooks is the cheapest and quickest fix, and it keeps backpacks off the floor at a height a child can reach. Mount a metal rail with three to five hooks at 40 to 48 inches for school-age children, higher for adults, and screw it into studs or use heavy-duty wall anchors, since a full backpack with books can weigh 15 pounds or more. Space hooks at least 8 inches apart so bags do not tangle. Choose rounded hooks that will not snag straps, and add a small shelf above for hats and keys. Adhesive hooks suit rentals but must be rated well above the bag's weight, and the wall paint needs to be clean and fully cured.
picks.best_for: Households that want a cheap, quick fix at child height
picks.quirky_fact: Wall hooks hold best when screws go into studs, which are usually spaced 16 inches apart.
picks.shop_query: wall mounted backpack hooks sturdy metal
picks.skip_if: Your walls are plaster or tile and you do not want to drill
picks.product_name: Heavy Duty Wall Mounted Coat Rack with 5 Hooks

picks.description: An over-the-door organizer uses the back of a door as storage, so it works where there is no wall space to spare. Hooks slip over the top edge and hold bags and jackets, and many include pockets for shoes, gloves or lunch boxes. Choose a model made for your door thickness, usually 1.5 to 1.75 inches, and check that the door still closes without scraping the frame. Metal-framed racks hold more weight than plastic ones, while fabric pocket organizers suit light items. A rubber stopper on the bottom stops the door from banging. These racks can mark paint or loosen hinges if overloaded, so spread weight evenly and keep each hook below its rated limit.
picks.best_for: Dorms, rentals and small closets with no spare wall
picks.quirky_fact: Most over-the-door hooks are made for standard interior doors, which are about 1.375 to 1.75 inches thick.
picks.shop_query: over the door backpack organizer with pockets
picks.skip_if: Your doors are thicker than standard or are glass or hollow-core
picks.product_name: Over the Door Hook Rack 6 Hooks Metal

picks.description: Stackable bins give each person a labeled place for a bag, shoes and jacket, which works well in a mudroom or hallway with floor room. Choose bins about 12 to 16 inches wide with open fronts or handles so children can pull them out without help. Give each person a color or a name label so nobody argues about whose is whose. Stacked two high, the bins take up little floor area, and a lid on the top bin makes a spot for keys and mail. Plastic is easiest to wipe clean after wet weather, while fabric or woven versions look better in a living space but hold dirt. Place a mat or tray underneath to catch mud and water.
picks.best_for: Families who want one assigned bin per person
picks.quirky_fact: Open-front bins let children see what is inside, which helps younger kids put things back without being asked.
picks.skip_if: Your entry is narrow and a floor stack would block the way
picks.product_name: Stackable Storage Bins with Handles Set of 4

picks.description: A freestanding stand holds several backpacks upright on pegs or arms and needs no drilling, which suits rentals and shared spaces. Look for a stand 50 to 70 inches tall with a wide, weighted base so it does not tip when loaded unevenly. Wood versions blend into a living area, while metal ones tolerate rough use in a mudroom. Count the hooks against the people who need them, and add one or two extra for visitors. Test stability with a full bag on the top hook before regular use, and keep it away from doorways where it could be bumped. Place a tray or mat on the floor beneath for wet shoes and an umbrella.
picks.best_for: Rentals and open spaces where wall mounting is not allowed
picks.quirky_fact: Coat-tree style stands usually have a heavy base because a loaded stand has a high center of gravity.
picks.skip_if: You have small children who could pull a tall stand over
picks.product_name: Freestanding Coat Rack with Shoe Bench and Hooks

picks.description: A wall shelf with hooks underneath combines a surface for keys, mail and sunglasses with a place to hang bags. Choose a shelf 24 to 36 inches wide with three to five hooks and mount it with screws into studs. The top holds a small basket or tray for loose items, and the hooks hold backpacks at a comfortable height. Keep the shelf shallow, around 6 to 8 inches, so it does not catch people walking past. A mixed set of rounded wood and black metal hooks suits most entryways, and a matching shelf with a lip stops items sliding off. Because hooks carry the load, check the rated capacity before hanging full bags.
picks.best_for: Entryways that need a drop spot for bags, keys and mail
picks.quirky_fact: Shelves with hooks are often sold as entryway sets because the top surface collects keys and small items.
picks.shop_query: hanging backpack storage shelf with hooks
picks.skip_if: Your wall space is limited by a door or a window at that height
picks.product_name: Entryway Wall Shelf with Hooks Wood 31 inch

picks.description: Fabric cubes fold flat when empty and hold a backpack, sports gear or spare bags in a closet or shelf unit. Choose cubes around 11 to 13 inches, which fit common cube shelves, and look for reinforced sides so they hold shape when full. Handles make them easy to slide out, and a label window helps in shared rooms. They are not the best choice for wet bags, since fabric can trap moisture, so use them for clean, dry storage. Fold them flat when not needed. A set of six with two colors lets you separate school bags from gym bags, and washable fabric means spills wipe clean.
picks.best_for: Closets and shelf units that need hidden, flexible storage
picks.quirky_fact: Cube-shaped bins are made to fit 13-inch shelving units, which are the most common cube size sold.
picks.skip_if: Bags come home wet from rain and need to air out
picks.product_name: Foldable Fabric Storage Cubes 11 inch Set of 6

picks.description: Strong magnetic hooks stick to a steel surface such as a locker, a metal door or the side of a refrigerator, with no drilling or adhesive. Choose a hook rated for at least twice the weight of a loaded bag and check that the surface is ferrous steel, since many doors are painted aluminum or wood and will not hold a magnet. Test with a full bag over a few days, and wipe both surfaces so grit does not let the hook slide. Rubber-coated magnets protect paint from scratches. They suit school lockers and garage walls well, but they are not a safe choice for heavy bags on a smooth door, where a slip can drop the load.
picks.best_for: Locker, garage and steel-door setups that cannot be drilled
picks.quirky_fact: A magnet only holds on iron or steel, so many modern doors and lockers made of aluminum will not work.
picks.skip_if: Your surface is wood, drywall or aluminum that magnets will not grip
picks.product_name: Heavy Duty Magnetic Hooks 100 lb Set of 4

picks.description: A multi-pocket fabric organizer hangs on a wall or door and holds backpacks, hats, gloves and shoes in one place. Look for stitched seams, reinforced hanging loops and pockets sized for a lunch box or a water bottle. Hang it at child height for easy access, and fill the bottom pockets with the heaviest items so the unit hangs flat. Fabric organizers sag when overloaded, so check the weight limit and spread the load across pockets. A clear front pocket helps you find items quickly. Machine wash or spot clean based on the label, and plan a weekly reset to clear out clutter so pockets do not become a junk drawer.
picks.best_for: Families that need to store small items with each bag
picks.quirky_fact: Clear pockets help children see what is inside, which reduces morning searching for gloves and hats.
picks.shop_query: multi pocket hanging backpack organizer fabric
picks.skip_if: A single large backpack per person is all you need to store
picks.product_name: Hanging Wall Organizer with Pockets Fabric

picks.breed: Entryway Bench with Built-in Backpack Storage
picks.description: A bench with cubbies or drawers provides seating, shoe storage and bag space in one piece, so it suits the main entrance of a family home. Check the width first, since a bench of 36 to 48 inches fits a typical hallway, and leave at least 36 inches of clear walkway beside it. Add hooks above the bench for bags and coats, and use baskets in the cubbies to hide clutter. Solid wood or engineered wood with a veneer suit most homes, but check the weight rating of the seat. Assembly can take an hour or two, so plan time and use a helper. Wipe the seat often, since it will collect mud and spills.
picks.best_for: Entryways with floor space and a need for seating
picks.quirky_fact: Benches with cubbies are often designed so each cubby holds a pair of shoes, which keeps the entryway floor clear.
picks.shop_query: entryway bench with backpack storage cubbies
picks.skip_if: Your hallway is narrower than 36 inches in total
picks.product_name: Entryway Storage Bench with Cubbies and Cushion

picks.description: A ceiling-mounted pulley rack lets you raise bags out of the way, which suits garages, workshops and rooms with high ceilings. A pulley system with a rope hoists the rack up and down, and a cleat on the wall keeps it secure. Anchor it into ceiling joists with proper hardware, since failure could drop the load. Check the weight rating and do not exceed it. This setup works best for off-season bags and sports gear rather than daily use, because daily lowering takes time. Keep it away from lights, fans and door swings. For a rental, check with the landlord first, since it needs permanent mounting and holes in the ceiling.
picks.best_for: Garages and high-ceiling rooms for rarely used bags
picks.quirky_fact: Pulley racks work like a block and tackle, which is why a small pull can lift a heavy load.
picks.shop_query: ceiling mounted pulley backpack rack metal
picks.skip_if: You rent, have low ceilings or need a bag every day
picks.product_name: Ceiling Storage Rack Pulley Hoist Garage

faqs.question: How do I store backpacks without drilling into walls?
faqs.answer: Use an over-the-door hook rack, a freestanding stand, stackable bins or a bench with cubbies. All of these work without holes. Adhesive hooks can work for light bags but must be rated far above a loaded backpack's weight, and the wall needs to be clean. Magnetic hooks work only on steel surfaces.

faqs.question: What height should backpack hooks be?
faqs.answer: For school-age children, mount hooks at roughly 40 to 48 inches from the floor so they can reach without help. Adults can go higher, around 60 inches. If children of different ages share a rail, hang two rows, one low and one high, so each person has a hook within reach.

faqs.question: How much weight can backpack hooks hold?
faqs.answer: It depends on the hook and the wall. Screwed into studs, many metal hooks hold 20 pounds or more, while adhesive ones may be rated for only a few pounds. Check the package rating and compare it to a full backpack, which can weigh 15 pounds or more with books and a laptop.

faqs.question: What is the best backpack storage for a small entryway?
faqs.answer: Wall hooks or a shallow shelf with hooks, because they take no floor space. An over-the-door rack is another option when the wall is occupied. Keep anything projecting from the wall under 8 inches deep so it does not catch passers-by, and add a tray on the floor for shoes.

topic_title: Backpack Storage Ideas: 10 Ways to Keep Bags Off the Floor
author: Elena Marsh
answer: For most homes, start with wall-mounted hooks at child height, add an over-the-door organizer where wall space is short, and use bins or a bench with cubbies if you have floor room. The deciding factor is where the bags land when people walk in, so store them there.
